title: Attention TNA
text: Regular TNA looks pairs states happen one right . student Plan time 3 Monitor time 4, TNA counts transition. ignores relationship Plan time 3 Adapt time 7. two events four steps apart, TNA treats unrelated. problem earlier events still matter later . student plans start session still influenced planning adapt several steps later. user’s first prompt chatbot conversation shapes responses several turns line. cases, connection two events real — ’s just immediate. ATNA fills gap. Instead counting adjacent transitions, looks pairs states across whole sequence weights far apart . Close events get high weight. Distant events get low weight. weight drops following exponential curve, nearby things matter lot far-away things matter little — still matter.

title: Attention TNA
text: Take sequence student actions: Regular TNA draws line pair neighbors: Plan→Monitor, Monitor→Discuss, Discuss→Emotion, . Seven events produce six edges. ATNA draws lines every pair, decreasing weight: Plan→Monitor (1 step apart): strong connection Plan→Discuss (2 steps apart): weaker Plan→Emotion (3 steps apart): weaker still Plan→Adapt (4 steps apart): faint Plan→Monitor (5 steps apart): faint Plan→Plan (6 steps apart): barely starting every event sequence. weighted connections get added across every sequence data. result weight matrix cell captures often state appears state B, weighted close together tend .
code: Plan → Monitor → Discuss → Emotion → Adapt → Monitor → Plan

title: Attention TNA
text: Centrality tells states play biggest role network. gives three measures state: InStrength: much attention flows state states. state high InStrength common destination — events tend followed , even several steps later. OutStrength: much attention flows state toward states. state high OutStrength long reach — happens, shapes comes across multiple future steps. Betweenness: often state sits shortest path states. state high betweenness acts bridge connecting different parts network. plot three:  makes bar chart states x-axis centrality scores y-axis, one panel per measure. Reading results: compare ATNA centralities tell ’d get regular TNA. state might low OutStrength TNA (doesn’t strongly predict next step) high OutStrength ATNA (broad, lasting influence across many future steps). kind state matters first-order analysis suggest.

text: Scaling change units weights, relative order. Plotting absolute weights scaled weights checks : compare() pairs edges two models scatterplot shows Pearson correlation weights. code: # Plotting the two weights together to see if the scaling distorts the data plot(   compare(model, model_scaled),   type = "scatterplot",   name_x = "Absolute",   name_y = "Scaled" ) # Calculate the Transition Network Analysis (TNA) on the `group_regulation`  # data with ranked weights model_ranked <- ftna(group_regulation, scaling = "rank") print(model_ranked) # Print the FTNA model with ranked weights # Compare the absolute and the ranked weights plot(   compare(model, model_ranked),   type = "scatterplot",   method = "spearman",   name_x = "Absolute",   name_y = "Ranked" )

text: Load package Example data Build Markov model Plot transition network Calculate centrality measures Plot centrality measures  Estimate centrality stability Identify plot communities  Find plot cliques  Compare high achievers (first 1000) low achievers (last 1000) Simple comparison vs. permutation test comparison  Compare centralities
code: library("tna") data("group_regulation", package = "tna") tna_model <- tna(group_regulation) summary(tna_model) plot(tna_model) cent <- centralities(tna_model) plot(cent, ncol = 3) estimate_centrality_stability(tna_model) #> Centrality Stability Coefficients #>  #>  InStrength OutStrength Betweenness  #>         0.9         0.9         0.9 coms <- communities(tna_model) plot(coms) cqs <- cliques(tna_model, threshold = 0.12) plot(cqs) tna_model_start_high <- tna(head(group_regulation, 1000)) tna_model_start_low <- tna(tail(group_regulation, 1000)) comparison <- permutation_test(   tna_model_start_high,    tna_model_start_low,   measures = c("InStrength") ) plot_compare(tna_model_start_high, tna_model_start_low) plot(comparison) summary(comparison, what = "centralities")

title: Bootstrap Transition Networks from Sequence Data — bootstrap
text: x tna group_tna object created sequence data. Grouped models scaled edge weights, networks, resampled (error class tna_error_scaling). iter integer specifying number bootstrap samples draw. Defaults 1000. level numeric value representing significance level hypothesis testing confidence intervals. Defaults 0.05. method character string. argument defines bootstrap test statistic. "stability" option (default) compares edge weights range "consistent" values defined consistency_range. Weights fall outside range considered insignificant. words, edge considered significant value within range (1 - level) * 100% bootstrap samples. "threshold" option instead compares edge weights user-specified threshold value. threshold numeric value compare edge weights . default 10th percentile edge weights. Used method = "threshold". consistency_range numeric vector length 2. Determines much edge weights may deviate (multiplicatively) observed values () considered insignificant. default c(0.75, 1.25) corresponds symmetric 25% deviation range. Used method = "stability". seed single numeric random seed reproducible resampling, NULL (default) use current RNG state. actor optional actor identifier sequences nested actors (example, several sessions per student). Either character string naming non-sequence column data model built (column meta_data prepare_data()), vector one identifier per sequence (per sequence data grouped model built , group_tna object). given, whole actors resampled replacement instead single sequences (cluster bootstrap; Davison & Hinkley, 1997, Section 3.8), sequences nested actors treated independent. default NULL resamples sequences.

title: Build a Transition Network Analysis Model — build_model
text: x stslist (TraMineR), data.frame, matrix, tna_data object (see prepare_data()), tsn object (long table columns id, state, time, produced tsn package). stslist data.frame objects x describe sequence events states used building Markov model.  x matrix, assumed element row column j weight edge representing transition state state j. x data.frame, must wide format (see cols define columns time points). ... Ignored. build_model aliases (e.g., tna), argument matches actual arguments build_model beside x. type character string describing weight matrix type. Currently supports following types: "relative" relative frequencies (probabilities, default) "frequency" frequencies. "co-occurrence" co-occurrences. "n-gram" n-gram transitions. Captures higher-order transitions considering sequences n states, useful identifying longer patterns. "gap" allows transitions non-adjacent states, transitions weighted gap size. "reverse" considers sequences reverse order (resulting called reply network contexts). resulting weight matrix transpose "frequency" option. "attention" aggregates downstream pairs states exponential decay gap states. parameter lambda can used control decay rate (default 1). scaling character vector describing scale weights defined type. vector provided, scaling options applied respective order. example, c("rank", "minmax") first compute ranks, scale unit interval using min-max normalization. empty vector corresponds scaling. Currently supports following options: "minmax" performs min-max normalization scale weights unit interval. Note smallest weight positive, zero scaling. "max" Multiplies weights reciprocal largest weight scale weights unit interval. options preserves positive ranks, unlike "minmax" weights positive. "rank" Computes ranks weights using base::rank() ties.method = "average". params list additional arguments models specific type. potential elements list : n_gram: integer n-gram transitions specifying number adjacent events. default value 2. max_gap: integer gap-allowed transitions specifying largest allowed gap size. default 1. windowed: Perform model estimation window. Supported relative, frequency co-occurrence types. window_size: integer sliding window transitions specifying window size. default 2. window_type: character string defines window type. Either "rolling" "tumbling". weighted: logical value. TRUE, transitions weighted inverse sequence length. Can used frequency, co-occurrence reverse model types. default FALSE. direction: character string specifying direction attention models type = "attention". available options "backward", "forward", "", backward attention, forward attention, bidirectional attention, respectively. default "forward". decay: function specifies decay weights two time points specific distance. function take three arguments: , j lambda, j numeric vectors time values, lambda  numeric value decay rate. function return numeric vector weights. default function(, j, lambda) exp(-abs(- j) / lambda). lambda: numeric value decay rate. default 1. time: matrix data.frame providing time values sequence time index. tna_data objects, can also logical value, TRUE use time_data element x time values. Date values converted numeric. duration: matrix data.frame providing time spent state sequence time index. alternative time. inits optional numeric vector initial state probabilities state. vector scaled unity. cols expression giving tidy selection columns considered sequence data. default, columns used. concat integer number consecutive sequences concatenate. default 1 (concatenation). begin_state character string additional begin state. state added first observation every sequence signify beginning sequence end_state character string additional end state. state added last observation every sequence signify end sequence.

title: Calculate Centrality Measures for a Transition Matrix — centralities
text: following measures provided: OutStrength: Outgoing strength centrality, calculated using igraph::strength() mode = "". measures total weight outgoing edges node. InStrength: Incoming strength centrality, calculated using igraph::strength() mode = "". measures total weight incoming edges node. ClosenessIn: Closeness centrality (incoming), calculated using igraph::closeness() mode = "". measures close node nodes based incoming paths. ClosenessOut: Closeness centrality (outgoing), calculated using igraph::closeness() mode = "". measures close node nodes based outgoing paths. Closeness: Closeness centrality (overall), calculated using igraph::closeness() mode = "". measures close node nodes based incoming outgoing paths. Betweenness: Betweenness centrality defined number geodesics calculated using igraph::betweenness(). BetweennessRSP: Betweenness centrality based randomized shortest paths (Kivimäki et al. 2016). measures extent node lies shortest paths nodes. Diffusion: Diffusion centrality Banerjee et.al. (2014). measures influence node spreading information network. Diffusion always min-max normalized range 0 1, whatever value normalize, raw values grow powers edge weights (frequency model easily exceed 1e30). raw values equal every state, example relative transition network loops = TRUE every row sums one, normalized values NaN: measure distinguish states. Clustering: Signed clustering coefficient Zhang Horvath (2005) based symmetric adjacency matrix (sum adjacency matrix transpose). measures degree nodes tend cluster together. PageRank: Weighted PageRank centrality calculated using igraph::page_rank() directed transition network.

title: Build a Random Mixture Markov Model Object — random_tna_mmm
text: n_clusters integer giving number mixture clusters. NULL (default), drawn 2:4 call. n_states integer >= 2 giving number states. NULL (default), value drawn 7:11 call. states optional character vector state labels length least n_states. first n_states used. NULL (default), labels taken category auto-picked built-pool fits n_states. category optional character string naming built-label pool. Available pools returned list_random_state_pools(). NULL (default), pool whose size least n_states sampled random. Ignored states supplied. alpha positive numeric Dirichlet concentration parameter. Small values (e.g. 0.3) produce sparse, peaked transitions; large values (e.g. 5) produce near-uniform transitions. NULL (default), value drawn Uniform(0.5, 1.0) call. diag_boost non-negative numeric added diagonal transition matrix re-normalising rows. Larger values make states "stickier" (self-transitions). NULL (default), value drawn Uniform(1.5, 3.0) call. n_sequences integer giving number sequences simulate true parameters. NULL (default), value drawn 500:800 call. seq_length integer giving length simulated sequence. NULL (default), value drawn 6:20 call. n_covariates integer >= 1 giving number regression variables (including intercept) used predict cluster membership. Default 1 (intercept ). > 1, additional rows added coefficient matrix. seed integer random seed reproducibility, NULL (default) fresh randomness every call.
